text:
Alex Park: Heads-up — ACME onboarding requires EU-first private deploy with an SLA ask (99.9% uptime) and p95 <200ms for chat. They asked for an automatic soft-fail path to a smaller quantized model if latency or cost becomes problematic. Need a concise rollout + fallback plan.
Priya Patel: We can do this with a per-tenant flag and a staged canary. Proposal: per-tenant feature flag (acme.eu_onboard). Canary ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over ~72h. Add a preflight smoke run (50 synthetic prompts) and telemetry gates (p95, 5xx, token-cost, eval delta).
Samir Rao: +1. Add traffic "shutters" so we can throttle ACME traffic gracefully. Also implement "grace tokens" to let in-flight requests finish during cutover. Need an ops runbook for auto vs manual fallback.
Jia Chen: Kill metrics suggestion: p95 > 350ms sustained for 15m OR 5xx rate > 1.0% OR eval quality delta > 4% vs baseline. Also abort if cost-per-request increases >25% over baseline for >30m.
Alex Park: Can we automate fallback sequence? Proposed order: route -> quantized variant -> cached prefix hits -> reduced-context mode -> shed non-critical features. Thoughts?
Priya Patel: We should. Sequence as a single state machine tied to the tenant flag. States: off, canary, auto-fallback, forced-fallback. Auto-fallback steps: (1) switch to quantized variant (same API surface), (2) reduce max_tokens to 512, (3) enable aggressive prefix caching, (4) page SRE and mark degraded in console.
Samir Rao: Flag naming: feature:tenant:acme:eu_deploy_state. Requirements: audit log for every transition and console double-confirm for forced-fallback. Also add a metric that counts how many requests used the fallback path.
Jia Chen: A/B idea — run 10% of ACME traffic on the quantized variant (B) during initial canary to measure live quality delta. Capture BLEU/ROUGE proxies and queue 100 human review samples in the first 24h.
Alex Park: Owners: Product = Priya (spec + rollout coord), Eng-runtime = Samir (routing, shutters, flag adapter), Eng-ML = Jia (quality gates, eval set), SRE = Alex (runbook & paging), Solutions Eng = Tom (customer ops).
Priya Patel: Draft launch checklist: flag config & schema, canary infra reserved, telemetry dashboards (p95, 5xx, token-cost, fallback-rate, eval-delta), preflight synthetic set, runbook with kill criteria, customer-facing docs, postmortem template. Target kickoff: start dev next week, soft launch target 2026-04-12.
Samir Rao: Operational notes: add a 2h quiet window after each ramp step before increasing percent. Grace-token budget: reserve ~300 tokens/sec for ACME to finish in-flight without circuit-tripping. I'll add shutters API to sprint. ETA for basic shutters + flag adaptor: 2026-03-30.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary toggles updated for acme: canary=1% at 2026-03-24T09:00Z by Priya.
Jia Chen: :thumbsup: I'll assemble the 50-sample synthetic set and the 100 live-review queue. Samir — please add telemetry hooks for eval-delta and fallback-rate.
Samir Rao: On it. Will instrument fallback-rate and a histogram for fallback latency.
Alex Park: Final call on abort timing: if kill metric fires during canary, do we rollback instantly or wait N minutes?
Priya Patel: Abort policy: if kill metric persists longer than 10 minutes and auto-fallback sequence has been applied (and didn't resolve), rollback to the previous stable variant instantly and open an incident. Re-open canary only after manual sign-off.
Jia Chen: Also snapshot ~200 random ACME sessions on failure to feed to the model team and include user-visible degradation banner in the API response for forced-fallback.
Tom Nguyen: I'll draft the customer ops playbook and ACME-facing SLA blurb (what fallback means for user experience).
Alex Park: Great — I'll turn this thread into a short spec doc and schedule a 30m sync to lock dates. Thanks all.
